utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I welcome you all back for -- I won't say the whole of this year but for the new year, and we look forward to moving along quickly toward the end of this trial. We have more reason for hope in that regard than we had when we finished at the end of last year. We are sitting this afternoon to deal essentially with pre-Defence matters with a view to commencement of the first of the Defence cases tomorrow. Now, we will commence the proceedings by looking at the motions that there are to be dealt with in this matter. In most cases they being motions that are still in the process of initial submissions being presented. The first of them that I'm aware of is the Defence motion on behalf of Mr. Boskoski for the admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis from a number of witnesses, I think, 11 all together. That was filed on the 21st of January, and yesterday a response was received from the Prosecution to that motion. There has, of course, not been time for the Chamber to give a decision in it. I wouldn't anticipate that there's any need for there to be mention of any particular matter about that motion. It will be dealt with on the basis of the written submissions. I see no sign of anybody anxious to say anything about it. Did I provoke you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You did, Your Honour. Simply to give an indication and to confirm the position of the Chamber that we do not think there is any reason to warrant the reply on our behalf. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The second is a motion of the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski for protective measures in respect of witnesses. That was filed on the 24th of January. There's not yet been a response to it. So we just noticed that it is in its early stages. The third is a motion concerning an expert witness of the -- it's a motion of the Boskoski Defence, filed pursuant to Rule 94 bis. It was filed on the 24th of January, and there has not yet been a compliance with all the procedural steps. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I may simply be mired in my usual confusion. That motion filed on 24th of January, wasn't that a Prosecution motion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It was and that only means that I got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's rare, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, that's a good way to start the year, Mr. Saxon, but we all know the truth of these matters. It was a Prosecution motion concerning the Boskoski Defence expert witness, and it was filed on the 24th of January, and it's nowhere near ready for decision. Is there any matter concerning it which either party feels they need to mention in oral submission at this point or will it be dealt with in the ordinary course on the written submissions? Nothing -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in the course of preparing a written response and we hope to be able to file it in the course of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next is a motion this time not by the Prosecution but by the Defence for Mr. Boskoski for the admission of exhibits from the bar table. It was filed only on the 25th of January. There has not yet been a response which, in the ordinary course, would need to be filed on or before the 8th of February. So, again, we must wait. Could the Chamber mention that quite obviously the earlier the responses can be filed, earlier than the last possible date, the earlier it will be possible to reach a decision and therefore people will be able to move on with greater certainty as to what is to be expected. Now, the last motion of which I'm presently aware is a motion filed by the Boskoski Defence on the 25th of January for disclosure; I think it is pursuant to Rule 66(B). There has been no response to that. Ah, the response now is in, yes. Is there any matter about that motion which either party feels they should raise at this point? Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply to indicate, Your Honour, again that we will not seek leave to file any reply in relation to that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's nothing further, Mr. Saxon, that you would wish to raise in that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With respect to that particular matter, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I think that covers the motions that are alive. As you can see, they have all happened in the last week. The earliest of them is just one week from its inception. So there'll be a little bit of activity over the next few days in respect of those, and the sooner we get responses, the sooner they'll be able to be dealt with. We now have an indication that there may be an issue concerning Rule 65 ter (G) to be raised at this pre-Defence conference by the Prosecution. Is that right, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With your leave, yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I may, could we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was a matter, I believe, Mr. Apostolski, concerning 92 bis motions that you thought you may need to raise. Is this a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Considering the motion as per Rule 92 bis and the statements that the Defence took from the witnesses, I can inform Their Honours that the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski has taken four 92 bis statements, and we are waiting for the translation of one of them to be finalised. We expect that today or tomorrow as we were informed by the CLSS, the translation will be completed, and immediately afterwards we will submit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I did notice in one of the papers that I've read that there were some issues that you were experiencing, Mr. Apostolski, concerning translation, but I think they have been resolved with time, are they? Were you having some difficulty with translations?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the statements were not translated, although they're brief. The statements -- the 92 bis statements were one page each, and we are waiting for the translation, although we had submitted on the 29th of December, 2007, the translation of the expert report of our expert that will come and testify before this Court, so we are waiting for that translation to be finished. Otherwise, all the written evidence that we had submitted to the CLSS were submitted by the end of December and we can inform the Court that there are five remaining documents that were not translated. We expect that they will be finished very soon by the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And while you're on your feet, the matter of the uploading into the electronic Court system of the documents you intend to rely on, is that something that is underway now?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is ongoing. And I don't think there will be any problems related to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it is actually underway now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Well, perhaps on the same two themes for the 92 bis statement, first, we would simply wish to indicate that ten out of eleven of our proposed statements have now been certified. We are waiting for the last one. They have also been uploaded in e-court and will be released very soon. Concerning translation issues we would also wish to indicate that there remains a number of documents which we have either sent to CLSS for verification/corrections and a number of new documents which have come in our possession and which have been sent to CLSS. A number of those documents, Your Honour, do not appear on our Rule 65 ter list as they have been provided to the Defence at a late stage. What we believe we will do in the near future is as soon as we obtain the official translations of those documents, we will file a motion seeking leave to add them to our Rule 65 ter and we will do so as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. There was a suggestion, Mr. Apostolski, that there may even be scope for a reduction in the number of witnesses you had contemplated calling from your Rule 65 ter list. Is that something you're able to be more clear about at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That was the next thing I wanted to speak about and inform the Court that in coordination my learned colleague from the Prosecution, and the -- in the agreement with the Prosecutor's office we will remove three witnesses from my list. And we are making additional researches and I can inform the Chamber that there is a possibility to further reduce our list for -- the witnesses, but we will need additional days to finish the additional investigations that my investigator is in charge of. I could tell you those other witnesses, M-2D-001, M-2D-002, and M-2D-003, regarding which the Prosecutor did not object their potential removal from the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that, and as soon as your investigations have been completed, you will be able to formalise those matters. Thank you. Is there any other matter which, first of all, Mr. Saxon, you would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux? Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps briefly only let me say that as the learned colleague Prosecutor stated thus far we're still using the names of our witnesses from the confidential list and tomorrow, in our opening statements we will use, instead of the names of the witnesses the number under which that witness is included in the 65 ter list. We are doing that for the simple reason that the witnesses have not given us final answer as to whether they will seek protective measures. So that we do not seek to move into a closed session at the moments when we are clarifying the contents of their testimony we will use the number under which they are in the list of proposed witnesses. Another thing that I wish to inform the Chamber about is that the Defence envisages that the witness number 4 from our list will testify for three and a half hours in the direct examination and three and a half hours in the cross-examination, and one hour in the re-direct; that would be the Defence`s proposal. The witness number 5 [sic] will also testify for three and a half hours in the direct examination, three and a half hours in the cross-examination and for one hour in the re-direct. The witness number 3 is proposed to testify for six hours in the direct examination, six hours in cross-examination, and two-hours in the re-direct. As for witness number 1, that would testify for four hours in the direct examination, for four hours in the cross-examination and for two hours in the re-direct. And the witness number 5, the Defence proposes that in the direct examination that witness testifies for seven hours, seven hours in the cross-examination, and additional two hours in the re-direct. We wanted just to indicate that the issue that the Prosecutor raised in the communication with the Defence, we wish to say that our evidence from the list are uploaded in the e-court system and they are here available from the hyperlink, so the Defence has no possibility and feels no need to have the evidence presented in a different fashion to both the Prosecutor and our colleagues. We thank the Chamber for informing us in a timely fashion that our first witness will start testifying on Thursday morning and I can say that the Defence will have its opening statements tomorrow and we don't expect that the opening statement will last for more than one session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there appears to be some confusion perhaps it is only in the English transcript but the English transcript of Ms. Residovic's explanation of how long each via voce Defence witness will take refers twice to witness number 5 and perhaps that was just a mistake, but perhaps we need to clarify whom is whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise if there was some confusion. Your Honours, I stated that I will indicate in my opening statements but also today when I'm indicating the viva voce witnesses and the durations of their testimonies, I used the numbers that appear before the name of the witness in our 65 ter list. And the witness number 4 from the 65 ter list, the number 4, our proposal is that there is three and a half hours in direct examination, three and a half hours in cross-examination and one hour in re-direct. Witness from that list, number 5, we propose again that his testimony last for three and a half hours in the direct examination, for three and a half hours in cross-examination and one hour in the re-direct. Witness from our 65 ter list, under the number 3, we propose would testify for six hours in the direct examination, six hours in the cross-examination, and two hours in the re-direct. Witness marked in our 65 ter list with the number 1, our proposal is that they testify for four hours in the direct examination, four hours in the cross-examination, and two hours in the re-direct. And the witness number 5 from our 65 ter list -- I apologise, number 2. This is where the confusion occurred. Number 2 in our 65 ter list, our proposal is that they testify for seven hours in the direct examination, seven hours in the cross-examination, and two hours in the re-direct. I think that now I spoke slowly enough so that it is interpreted and that I corrected the error that I made with the final viva voce witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was there anything that you wished to raise, Mr. Apostolski, that has not been dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. At this time I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber did notice that in estimating the time that each witness might take the Boskoski Defence rather ambitiously calculated that we sit for four and a half hours in court each day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four hours a day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Four. Well, your written 65 ter brief footnotes at four and a half hours. And it seemed that the Tarculovski Defence was working on about three and a quarter hours. The Chamber, with the best will in the world only seems to be able to get three and three quarter hours out of a day, so if that could be borne in mind. The calculations and estimates clearly may need some adjustment, but the overall indications given by each Defence are, of course, very encouraging as to the speed with which we can anticipate to deal with the Defence cases and certainly much more encouraging than had earlier been anticipated, so we look forward to that. If there is no other matter, we are to sit tomorrow morning to hear the opening submissions, and we hear the first of the Boskoski Defence witnesses commencing Thursday morning. We thank you for your attendance and assistance, and we will adjourn now, to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of January, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.15 p.m.,
